title: Number Quest Unit 6 · The Building Yard (Explorer)

items.q: Which shape is NOT a quadrilateral?
misconceptions: a square has 4 sides, so it is a quadrilateral
correct
a rectangle has 4 sides, so it is a quadrilateral
a rhombus has 4 sides, so it is a quadrilateral
items.why: Quadrilateral means four sides. A square, a rectangle and a rhombus all have 4 sides; a triangle has only 3.

items.q: Which shape has no parallel sides at all?
misconceptions: both pairs of sides are parallel in a rectangle
both pairs of sides are parallel in a square
parallel is in its name: both pairs run side by side
correct
items.why: Rectangles, squares and parallelograms all have parallel sides. A triangle's sides all meet, so none of them run parallel.

items.q: A square is a kind of rectangle. Why is that true?
choices: It is bigger than other rectangles
It has 4 sides and 4 square corners, like every rectangle
It has 4 equal sides, and rectangles never do
misconceptions: size is not what makes a shape family
correct
a square itself is a rectangle with 4 equal sides, so rectangles can
names do not decide families; properties do
items.why: A family is decided by properties. Every rectangle has 4 sides and 4 square corners, and a square has both, so a square belongs in the rectangle family.

items.q: A garden is 6 meters long and 4 meters wide. What is its area?
misconceptions: that is the perimeter: the fence, not the carpet
added the sides instead of multiplying them
correct
multiplied and then added the sides as well
items.why: Area is the carpet: multiply the sides. 6 x 4 = 24 square meters. (Adding around the edge, 20, would give the perimeter.)

items.q: A square painting has sides of 5 inches. What is its perimeter?
misconceptions: counted only two of the four sides
counted only three of the four sides
that is the area: 5 x 5 counts the squares inside
correct
items.why: Perimeter walks all the way around: 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 = 20 inches. (25 would be the area, the squares inside.)

items.q: A rug is 8 feet long and 3 feet wide. Which pair is right?
misconceptions: swapped the two answers: 24 is the area, not the fence
11 is one length plus one width, only half the fence
correct
11 is the half-way measure, not the count of squares inside
items.why: Fence first: 8 + 3 + 8 + 3 = 22 feet of perimeter. Carpet second: 8 x 3 = 24 square feet of area.

items.q: Two roads on a map run side by side and never cross. What kind of lines are they?
misconceptions: perpendicular lines cross at a square corner
correct
a ray is a part of a line with one end, not a way two lines sit
these roads are straight, not curved
items.why: Lines that run side by side and never meet are parallel. Perpendicular lines are the ones that cross at a square corner.

items.q: Which letter folds exactly in half, both sides matching?
misconceptions: the top and bottom arms differ, so F cannot fold onto itself
the open side has no matching part
correct
the hook has no matching side
items.why: The letter A folds along a line down its middle: the two halves match exactly. F, G and J have parts with nothing to fold onto.

items.q: A treasure hides at the point (4, 2) on a grid. Starting at (0, 0), how do you walk to it?
misconceptions: swapped the pair: the first number always names the rightward walk
correct
the second number counts steps up, never down
added the pair together instead of walking each part
items.why: In a grid address, the first number counts steps right and the second counts steps up: (4, 2) is 4 right, then 2 up.
